issue: Does the statutory maximum default term of supervised release under 18 U.S.C. § 3583(b) cap the term for offenses under 21 U.S.C. § 841(b)(1), or does the 2002 'notwithstanding' clause in § 841(b)(1) allow a term of life?

sides.position: Life is the maximum term of supervised release for § 841(b)(1) offenses; the shorter default maximums of § 3583(b) do not apply.
cases: United States v. Jackson, 559 F.3d 368 (5th Cir. 2009)
United States v. Johnson, 331 F.3d 962 (D.C. Cir. 2003)

sides.position: Pre-2002 rule: § 3583(b) caps supervised release for § 841(b)(1) offenses, so the term cannot exceed the § 3583(b) default maximum. The opinion says this circuit held this before 2002 and has not yet addressed the effect of the 2002 amendment.
cases: United States v. Carlos Perez, 22 F.4th 430 (4th Cir. 2022)

this_court: does not decide (the excerpts describe the circuit's earlier cap rule and state that it has yet to confront the 2002 amendment's implications)
